solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Foremost of ladies always will take time to make purchase

indicators.note: the letters so far 'take' the next piece on after them
the foremost letter of a word is the one standing at its front

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
always = ever
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Women who always take their time over buying something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' is not buying here but a noun meaning grip or mechanical advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase is a firm hold or advantage gained, which is what leverage is.

clue.text: News of the French sports fixture

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)
a Test match, as in cricket or rugby

explanation.surface: A report on a French sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international match between national teams, especially in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The latest' is the most recent news, as in 'what's the latest?'.

clue.text: Val literally a hooligan!

indicators.note: reading the split name to the letter means writing out the joining word between its two parts, not just understanding it

parts.note: the name, split after its first letter
the joining word between the two parts of the name, set down as a word rather than understood

explanation.surface: Someone called Val is described as a real hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literally' asks you to take VAL as V and AL and set down those words to the letter, which spells V-AND-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wilfully damages property, a hooligan.

clue.text: Capital's co-founder rebuilt our slum

indicators.note: a slum that is rebuilt has its parts put together in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A city's founding father has redeveloped our slum district.
explanation.walkthrough: Legend says Romulus and his twin Remus founded Rome, hence 'co-founder' of a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Romulus is the legendary co-founder of Rome, Italy's capital.

clue.text: Fail to visit one of the fortifications

definitions.meaning: the idiom for a business being ruined or going under
taken literally: to go to one of the walls of a fortified place

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: to go to a wall of a fortified town.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Go to the wall' is an idiom for a business failing or going bust.

clue.text: Hangover from the freeze

parts.note: the surface pushes the morning-after headache; the setter means a thing that hangs over an edge
what a spell of freezing weather leaves dangling from gutters and eaves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangover' suggests the morning after; read it as something that hangs over, left behind by a freeze.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle hangs down from eaves and is left over from freezing weather.

clue.text: Disease is caught — cut short holiday time

indicators.note: cutting the word short leaves only its opening letters

parts.note: c is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a deletion: HOLIDAY cut short, with its last four letters removed
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone caught a disease and had to end their holiday early.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'cut short holiday' look like the consequence; it is instruction for trimming the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: cholera is one particular infectious disease, so the general word stands for it.

clue.text: Make a hash of meal back in US picnic

indicators.note: making a hash of something is making a mess of it, jumbling its order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Messing up the food at an American outdoor party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal signal, but it is simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A clambake is an American seaside picnic where clams and other food are baked.

clue.text: Alien comes to create upset and so on

indicators.note: the alien arrives first and the next piece follows

parts.note: E.T., the film's extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: upsetting CREATE knocks its letters out of order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An alien arrives and causes trouble, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Create upset' reads as 'cause trouble'; CREATE is really the fodder and 'upset' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Et cetera is Latin for 'and the rest', used to mean 'and so on'.

clue.text: Thin mist obscured metalworker

indicators.note: what is obscured is blurred out of its clear form

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A worker in a forge is hidden by a light haze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscured' seems to describe the mist hiding someone; it is the signal to rearrange THIN MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinsmith makes and repairs things from tin and other light metals.

clue.text: New Testament taken from monastic rambling of Biblical character?

indicators.note: rambling letters wander from their places
N and T are taken away from the longer word

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for the New Testament
MONASTIC with N and T removed

explanation.surface: Scripture quoted in a rambling monk's talk about a figure from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: 'Mosaic' is an adjective meaning 'of Moses', a Biblical character.
explanation.definitionFit: Mosaic means relating to Moses, as in the Mosaic law, so it describes something of a Biblical character.

clue.text: Try to include the whole vegetable

indicators.note: 'to include' tells the attempt word to take the whole in among its own letters, as a list includes an item

parts.note: have a shot = make an attempt
the whole = all

explanation.surface: Advice to cook the vegetable whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the noun, a shot or attempt, not the verb it seems to be.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like vegetable.

clue.text: Basil with group outside, getting fizzy drink

indicators.note: the group goes around the basil

parts.note: a set is a group
basil is a herb

explanation.surface: A man named Basil, with friends outside, buys a fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Basil looks like a man's name; it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet in the old sense is a sweet effervescent drink, and also the fizzy powder used to make one.

clue.text: Splendid to be seen with Parisian here in Cornish river, on the surface

indicators.note: the first piece is accompanied by what follows

parts.note: super = splendid

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
ici is French for 'here'

explanation.surface: A lovely scene with a Parisian on the surface of a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county at the south-west tip of England; its River Fal flows into the sea at Falmouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Superficial means on or affecting only the surface.

clue.text: One's not conscious of his progress

definitions.text: One's not conscious of his progress

parts.note: reads as someone unaware or ignorant; the setter means literally asleep
reads as advancement in life; the setter means his steps as he moves along

explanation.walkthrough: 'Progress' suggests advancement in life; read it literally as walking forward, which a sleepwalker does unaware.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleepwalker moves about while asleep, unconscious of where he is going.

clue.text: Insincere pair confronted

parts.note: a pair is two
confronted = faced

explanation.surface: Two hypocrites meet face to face.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first and the two synonyms follow in the order the answer reads.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone two-faced shows one face while holding another view, which is insincerity.

clue.text: Man on top of island's mountain

indicators.note: in a down answer the man sits on top of the island

parts.note: a man's name
Nevis is a Caribbean island; the 's is just linking grammar

explanation.surface: A climber stands on the summit of an island's peak.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a Caribbean peak; the answer is Britain's highest mountain, in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in the British Isles.

clue.text: Vehicle taking wife and cad to Cumbrian town

indicators.note: the vehicle picks up each piece in turn

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for wife
a heel is a cad, a dishonourable man
Barrow-in-Furness is a town in Cumbria, north-west England

explanation.surface: Someone drives his wife and a scoundrel to a town in the Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: The vehicle looks like a car or bus, but it is pushed by hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A wheelbarrow is a small hand-pushed vehicle for carrying loads.

clue.text: Letting outspoken general make notes

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the general's name gives the sound we need

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general; LEA is said the same
singing is making musical notes

explanation.surface: A frank military man is allowed to jot things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make notes' suggests writing; the notes are musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the property sense: letting a flat and leasing it both mean renting it out to a tenant.

clue.text: Firmly established source on film location

indicators.note: in a down answer the source sits on the location

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a film set

explanation.surface: A reliable informant is placed at a filming location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source' reads as an informant; here it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a batsman or an institution that is well set has settled in and cannot easily be shifted.

clue.text: Kay and I with Gail travelling from African city

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move out of place

parts.note: Kay is how the letter K is spelt out
used as is
used as is

explanation.surface: Two friends and I travel with Gail on a trip from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Kay looks like a second woman's name; it is the spelt-out name of the letter K.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Rwandan capital is one of the continent's cities.

clue.text: Grand being on top, and on Queen's aircraft

indicators.note: the next piece sits on the Queen

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds
a lid is a top
ER, Elizabeth Regina; the 's is linking grammar

explanation.surface: A great person riding high on the Queen's plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On top' reads as a phrase meaning 'in charge'; 'top' alone is a lid.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an engineless plane that rides air currents is one kind of aircraft.

clue.text: Bird enthusiast wants dog

indicators.note: the enthusiast wants the dog next to him

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast
to dog or tail someone is to follow them

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher would like a pet dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' looks like the animal; it is the verb, to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a pigeon or flycatcher with a fan-shaped tail.

clue.text: Double misfortune, receiving Western hostility

parts.note: ill = misfortune, written twice
the standard abbreviation for western

explanation.surface: Twice unlucky, a Westerner meets hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill' as a noun means harm or misfortune, as in 'for good or ill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: bearing someone ill will is feeling hostile towards them.

clue.text: Collapse caused by calcium meeting blood vessel?

indicators.note: the calcium meets the vessel and joins it

parts.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
a vein is a blood vessel

explanation.surface: A medical collapse brought on by calcium deposits in a vein.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is medical; the collapse is of a roof or tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a roof or tunnel that falls inwards is said to cave in, verb for verb with the definition.

clue.text: Emergency measures to make tree steady

parts.note: a fir is a tree
staid = steady, sober

explanation.surface: Urgent steps taken to stop a tree toppling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steady' reads as a verb, to prop up; it is the adjective, staid.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the emergency treatment given before professional help arrives.

clue.text: Signed revised plan

indicators.note: a revised word is reworked into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An amended scheme has been signed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revised plan' reads as one phrase; 'revised' belongs with SIGNED and 'plan' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name the scheme drawn up before something is built or made.

clue.text: Shopkeeper disinclined to get in ground rice

indicators.note: ground rice is broken up and mixed

parts.note: the letters to rearrange, becoming CIER
loth = unwilling, disinclined

explanation.surface: A grocer who can't be bothered to stock ground rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground rice' looks like a single ingredient; 'ground' is the signal to rearrange RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothier is someone who makes or sells clothes.
